findings.F1: The deeper the hourly plunge, the larger the next-day rebound, but only when the coin is already volatile against its own history. For a drop beyond 3 multiples of its 30-day mean absolute daily move, the next 24 hours, net of drift, are +956 bps (t 5.7, 55 independent cases, strength 1.95) when that 30-day level is over 1.4 times the coin's median, +173 bps (t 2.3, 85) between 1.0 and 1.4 times, and +13 bps (t 0.4, 236) below its median; drops of 2 to 3 multiples follow the same order (+215, +21, −3 bps).
findings.F2: Ranking drops of more than 1 multiple by depth times relative volatility, which is close to the drop in percent over the coin's long-run usual daily move, only the top fifth stands out. It gives +196 bps over 24 hours (t 5.6, 615 cases, strength 0.39), about 10 times the 19 bps cost of a round trip. The other four fifths give −9 to +34 bps (t ≤ 1.6).
findings.F3: The volatile-plunge rebound holds on every coin but not in every year. Drops of more than 1 multiple at relative volatility above 1.4 rebound +96 to +259 bps over 24 hours on all 6 coins (t 2.3 to 2.5 on five, 1.1 on XMR). By year they are positive in 2018 to 2021 and 2025 (+122 to +292 bps) and flat or negative in 2022 to 2024 (−32 to +2 bps).
findings.F4: The tested idea's weak overall size (0.020 strength, t 1.92) comes from mixing a strong tail with a dead middle. Drops beyond 3 multiples rebound +187 bps (t 4.6, 376 cases), while drops of 2 to 3 multiples give +39 bps (t 1.7). Measured by year, the beyond-3 group is −85 bps in 2022 and about 0 in 2023 and 2024, the calm years.
findings.F5: The rebound after a deep plunge is spread over the day rather than front-loaded. Of the +201 bps raw 24-hour move after drops beyond 3 multiples, +53 bps comes in the first 6 hours.
findings.F6: The book's worst days are the coin's crash days, and the coin rises the day after. In the book's worst decile of days, the book returns −393 bps while the coin falls −663 bps, and the coin then gains +79 bps the next day. This matches the idea buying into falls that are still under way.
findings.F7: Small fresh falls continue rather than revert. A 24-hour drop of 0 to 1 multiple is followed by −21 bps over the next 24 hours (t −3.1, 4991 cases).
findings.F8: Fridays stand out among weekdays, but a weekday is not a graded situation, so it gives no idea here. The 24-hour return net of drift is +49 bps on Fridays (t 4.9, 2333 cases; positive on all 6 coins and in 6 of 8 years), −43 bps on Mondays (t −3.8) and −36 bps on Thursdays (t −3.0).
findings.F9: A large 7-day rise as a multiple of the usual daily move is followed by more rise (+158 bps over 3 days, t 2.6, 353 cases), but it fails the robustness checks. It is negative on LTC (−115 bps) and in 2019 and 2022, so given the many angles examined it does not count as a finding to act on.

ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour return, read at an hourly close, is a drop several times its 30-day average absolute daily return while that 30-day average itself is high relative to the coin's own past year, the price rises over the next 1 day by more than its normal 1-day drift. The deeper the drop in multiples and the higher the 30-day average stands against the past year, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader should buy a deep hourly plunge for a day mainly when the coin is already in a volatile spell, because the rebound there is many times the cost of a trade, and treat the same plunge in a calm spell as no reason to trade.
ideas.name: volatile-spell plunge next-day rebound

ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour return, read at an hourly close, is a drop several times its average absolute daily return over the past year, the price rises over the next 1 day by more than its normal 1-day drift. The larger the drop in those multiples, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader should size a one-day rebound buy by how large the drop is against the coin's long-run daily move rather than its last month's, because only the drops that are large on that scale rebound by several times the cost of a trade.
ideas.name: long-scale plunge next-day rebound
